correctionNoteStructuralHold:
THE STRUCTURAL-TRANSITION HOLD. Marathon prescription changes, so the audit counts change with it, and every one of them moves DOWN except two that are explained below.

WHAT WAS WRONG. "The week a purpose arrives is a week the doses hold" existed in the runtime and had never fired: it compared mWeek.qSlots and mWeek.supportDays -- the BLOCK's constants, the same every week -- against mPrevQSlots and mPrevSupportDays, which were assigned from those same constants two lines later. Neither comparison could ever be true. The week's real structure is decided afterwards, by the capacity gate. The weekly-load instrument at 5d8716d is what found it.

WHAT REPLACED IT. The week is solved TWICE. Once at the doses this step of the progression offers; and where that week would give the athlete a structure they have never been prescribed -- another running day, a first or second quality session, or marathon-specific work entering the long run -- again around the same structure at the workload they have already earned. The second answer is what they receive. The block carries the number of steps ACTUALLY TAKEN rather than a week counter, so a held week costs one step; the rate is fixed at the block's solve and never re-derived, so no later week can be walked faster to make it up. There is no debt and no catch-up: measured across the valid population, the progression index never advances more than one step in a week.

MEASURED: 395 structural arrivals, 383 held at the earned workload, 12 not held because holding would have refused the very session that arrived, 0 retriggers of an established structure. 351 of the 383 held the long run exactly; the rest are Peak weeks, where the peak exposure is chosen by the phase and not by the progression. 367 arrivals still moved the week's total up, median +2.2km -- that is session geometry, chiefly a second or third supporting run that cannot be written below EASY_MIN_KM.

AND A CUTBACK IS A REDUCTION. The taper already had a ladder for a week that comes out larger than the one before it; a cutback needs the same one, because its doses come from the ordinary progression while the week before it may have been suppressed by a hold. Cutback weeks larger than their predecessor: 47 before the hold existed, 77 with it, 10 with the ladder -- all at 6-8km/week where the supporting runs are already at the floor.

THE LOAD-PROGRESSION FAMILIES, marathon, production-valid domain, 5d8716d -> here: compound_load_progression 162 -> 75; exceeds_two_week_backstop 58 -> 18; broad_load_increase 48 -> 24; quality_structure_step 240 -> 164; long_run_step_above_rate 137 -> 103; structure_introduced_with_dose_step 304 -> 291; and the descriptive percentage 441 -> 342. rebound_exceeds_trend rises 125 -> 162 and is arithmetic rather than load: a rebound is measured against the week before the cutback, and that week is now sometimes a held one, so the ratio to it is larger while the sessions still step at the same fixed rate.

structure_introduced_with_dose_step barely moves because the audit is right to keep reporting it. Its 291 survivors decompose into 61 checkpoint weeks (a pinned measurement whose day is a time trial plus its flanks, not a new structure), 57 first-quality weeks whose session is simply larger than the supporting run it replaced, 46 running-day arrivals where EASY_MIN_KM forces the week up, and 16 medium-long arrivals, which the DAY builder decides and the week-level hold therefore cannot reach. Median +1 to +3.6km each.

EVERY VALID-DOMAIN INVARIANT IS UNCHANGED AT ZERO: long_run_shorter_than_quality, long_run_shorter_than_easy_run, volume_unattributed, long_run_zero_distance, zero_km_work_segment, generator_invariant_failure, quality_dominates_week, week_one_exceeds_stated_volume, week_overshoots_target_declared, taper_week_increases_volume.
correctionNoteEntrySafety:
week_one_exceeds_stated_volume IS RETIRED AND REPLACED BY week_one_exceeds_entry_capacity, AT ZERO.

IT ASKED THE RIGHT SAFETY QUESTION UNDER THE WRONG AUTHORITY. "Week one is more than 30% above the volume the athlete STATED" reads a typed weekly figure as the thing week one must respect, and that is the authority destination-led construction removed: the engine reads demonstrated evidence first, the typed figure second, and the pathway's own entry assumption last. An athlete with a year of 60km weeks who types 20 was not protected by holding week one to 26; they were mis-measured.

THE REPLACEMENT ASKS THE SAME QUESTION OF WHATEVER THE BLOCK ACTUALLY OPENED FROM, in that order, reading the provenance the block now records on every week (bottomUp.origin.volumeSource). There is no loophole in the absence of evidence: an athlete who states nothing is held to the PATHWAY's entry week, a figure they did not supply and cannot inflate.

AND A FLOOR IS NOT A PROGRESSION. The 170 surviving cases are all at stated volumes of 1-4km/week, all below the Race Goal entry boundary of 6, and in every one the week is exactly its sessions' own minimums: a long run and a supporting run at EASY_MIN_KM is a 6km week whatever anybody intended. They are recorded as week_one_at_session_floor under `descriptive`, which is how floor excess is treated everywhere else in this instrument, rather than counted as an entry failure they are not.

THE SERIES, FOR COMPARABILITY: week_one_exceeds_stated_volume ran 404 -> 150 -> 360 on the destination-led branch, where the pathway's entry long run was being applied to athletes far below the pathway's entry week. Scaling that assumption by the athlete's own stated week brought it to 170, and every one of those 170 is a floor state. The hard class is zero across the whole population, not only inside the race domain.

IN THE POPULATION THE PRODUCT BUILDS, EVERY FAMILY IS UNCHANGED OR LOWER. The rises are confined to the routed population -- cases where the race generator is probed at a stated volume far below the viable start for that event, and where the product delivers a foundation block and an on-ramp before any race block exists. Those are defensive states, and they are exactly the states in which a programme that now travels from an 8km entry to a 26km requirement has the furthest to go.

WHY THEY ROSE, IN ONE SENTENCE: the blocks arrive now. Every pathway used to finish its Peak at 70-90% of its own requirement, because the progression curve completed at a step no week stood on; the weeks were therefore flat, and flat weeks are quiet. A block that walks from the athlete's entry to the event's requirement steps at the ordinary rate in most of its weeks, and each of these families counts weeks that step.

WHAT WAS FIXED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED, and each is measured in its own commit: the absorption week no longer lands on the block's durability exposure or the week before it (the largest single step in the population falls from 23.5km to 20.5, and the >10km transition class from 121 to 28); the marathon no longer reaches its longest run by jumping to it; a reduction week can no longer introduce a session; the structural hold belongs to the session the arrival is in; and the week-level top-up serves the event's requirement rather than the athlete's own demonstrated volume, which was ratcheting the programme half a kilometre a year forever.

WHAT WAS TRIED AND REJECTED: bounding each quality family's growth to sessionProgressionRate() against its own high-water mark. It reduced quality_structure_step by 31 and compound by 46, and it cost the half its most specific Peak session -- 11.2km becoming 7.9 in the week the block exists to rehearse. A count is not worth a session.

FOUR CLASSES CLOSED COMPLETELY in the same pass: zero_km_work_segment, long_run_zero_distance and generator_invariant_failure 348 -> 0, and week_one_exceeds_stated_volume is retired for week_one_exceeds_entry_capacity at 0. See correctionNoteEntrySafety.

EXPERIENCE-SPECIFIC PHASE GEOMETRY. The same fifteen weeks, allocated differently by pathway: an advanced athlete arrives with the week already built, so two weeks of Base is re-establishment and a threshold reading rather than construction; a novice marathoner's binding constraint is the long run, which develops in Build. Base 4/4/2 -> 3/4/2 for the marathon and 3/3/2 for the half; Peak never moves, because it is what makes the block preparation for this event rather than continued training.

THE MATRIX BUILDS FROM DEFAULT STATE, where the athlete's level is 'experienced' and both events' shapes are unchanged -- so the whole population should have been byte-identical, and one family moved by eleven. The cause is a correction that came with the threading rather than the geometry: marathonSlotKindFor() and the day builder both re-derived the phase counts from marathonPhaseAllocation(), which gave a HALF block the marathon's four-week Base. Both now read the counts the block was actually allocated, which it carries for exactly this reason -- an allocation that depends on the athlete cannot be re-derived by a caller that does not know them. structure_introduced_with_dose_step 769 -> 780, entirely in the routed population; the race population is unchanged at 76, and long_run_step_above_rate falls there from 23 to 22.
correctionNoteEntryGeometry:
HQ'S LOCKED WEEK-1 ENTRY, THE STEP COUNT THAT HAD TO CHANGE WITH IT, AND THE
THREE THINGS THAT FELL OUT. Same 2,350 plans, same 30,080 weeks, same inputs.

WHAT CHANGED IN THE RUNTIME. (1) The bottom-up arc was seeded at step one, so
week one was delivered one progression step ABOVE the athlete's entry -- 22.5km
for a locked 20km novice marathon start. The code said why: seeded at zero the
last developing week stood on step P-1 of P. That is the count being wrong, not
the start: P weeks contain P-1 intervals. Week one now IS the entry and the step
count is the count of gaps. (2) Race-specific work arriving in the week after an
absorption week held its dose there, giving two consecutive weeks on the same
step; the arrival now waits a week where it would land there. (3) A governed
long run no longer absorbs supporting volume the easy days cannot hold: on a
three-day 24-week half the block asked for an 11.3km long run in week ten and
the athlete was written a 16km one, a 45% single-week step invisible to the
curve. That volume is now surrendered and reported as undistributedKm.

WHAT CHANGED IN THE INSTRUMENT, and it is one units error rather than a
threshold. REBOUND_EXCEEDS_TREND compared a change spanning two weeks against a
one-week ceiling. Once the curve began stepping THROUGH an absorption week --
which every published methodology does, and which this branch corrected -- a
rebound landed at 1.10 squared by construction and was reported as an overshoot.
It is now raised to the number of weeks the comparison actually spans. A rebound
that genuinely outruns two weeks of trend still fires: 57 of them do.

AND ONE ORDERING. week_one_exceeds_entry_capacity read demonstrated, then the
STATED weekly figure, then the pathway. The engine stopped reading the typed
number as an entry authority when destination-led construction removed it, so
the middle term measured the block against a figure it is ruled not to use and
reported 161 race programmes as opening above an entry that was never theirs.
The typed figure is still measured, as the descriptive class
week_one_above_stated_volume -- 476 cases, 146 of them race programmes -- because
the gap between what an athlete says they run and what their chosen pathway
opens at is a real thing a reader should see. It is an open question for HQ,
not a resolved one.

THE SUPPORTING WORKLOAD NO LONGER FALLS BEHIND THE LONG RUN IT SUPPORTS.

Two counters were split earlier on this branch so that the long run stepped
through an absorption week and the supporting workload did not. The reason was
real -- every session in the week taking two steps across a down week at once
produced a 32.5km single-week rise -- but the repair was in the wrong place. It
made the supporting curve fall one step behind the long run at EVERY cutback,
cumulatively: three cutbacks in a fifteen-week block left the long run 1.10
cubed ahead of the running under it. Measured on the experienced marathon, the
Peak week arrived with supporting runs at 28% of a 29km long run against the
40% SUPPORT_SHARE_MIN that marathonSupportDestination() reads in exactly this
direction. Two sessions whose destinations are defined relative to each other
cannot be developed on curves that diverge by construction.

The 32.5km rise was a symptom of the step COUNT, which this branch has since
corrected: with the count right, the largest single-week rise anywhere in the
population is 9.6km, so the split is no longer holding anything up. Removed, the
two curves are the same curve again and the Peak supporting share rises to 36%.
The two-week backstop stays at zero across all five distances and every pathway
still reaches its destination.

IT DOES NOT CLOSE THE COHERENCE GAP, and that is reported rather than papered
over. 36% is still short of 40%, and the diagnosis is that the pathway's own
numbers cannot reach it: a 29km long run needs two supporting runs of 11.6km,
which with a quality session is a 65km week against the 55km the experienced
marathon pathway states. That is a question about a locked figure and therefore
HQ's to rule on. test/marathonPeakViability.test.js asserts 40% and is LEFT
FAILING deliberately: weakening it would hide the finding, and the finding is
the point.

correctionNoteFrequencyRepairII:
RACE GOAL HALF/MARATHON FREQUENCY REPAIR II. ZERO COUNTERS MOVE AT THE WHOLE-POPULATION SCALE; EVERY CLASS IN THIS RECORD, INCLUDING EVERY RATCHETED DEFECT, IS UNCHANGED.

THE DEFECT. mNeed's own repair (test/raceGoalFrequencyArchitecture.test.js) correctly turned it from a ceiling into a floor, but the day count it could ever GROW TO stayed bound by SUPPORT_SHARE_MIN read as an EQUAL per-day share of a Half/Marathon-scale long run (26-32km for a marathon) -- and dividing the same supporting workload across more days always shrinks the average share, so a marathon week routinely stalled at 2-3 support days regardless of real selected availability. Live symptom: a 6-selected-day Marathon Build week resolved to 4 definite runs (2 easy + 1 quality + 1 long) + 1 Optional + 2 Rest, with two of the six selected days genuinely unused.

THE FIX TOUCHES NOTHING THAT SIZES OR TOTALS A WEEK. SUPPORT_SHARE_MIN, mSupportDays, mSupportDest, longDestKm, qSlots and every weekly volume total are exactly as they were -- proven directly (see test/raceGoalFrequencyRepairII.test.js's 'weekly destination volume is unchanged' and 'long run and quality-session sizes are unchanged' tests). distributeWeekVolume() (shared, pre-existing) already redivides a week's FIXED easy budget safely down to its own floor, EASY_MIN_KM, whenever more calendar easy-day slots are offered to it -- the day count reaching it (runCap) was simply never allowed past SUPPORT_SHARE_MIN's stricter number. raceGoalDestinationSolve() now also returns scheduledSupportDays (informational, block-level); buildBlockWeeks() computes the real, per-week, capacity-respecting version once each week's own supportDays has settled through marathonSupportDaysFor()'s structural-progression ramp and any taper/cutback/give-back reduction -- widening THIS week's own earned day count toward HQ's contract (N selected -> at least N-1 definite), never a flat block-level number, and never past what the week has itself earned to grow to. Gated on distKey so 5K/10K are provably untouched (test/raceGoalFrequencyRepairII.test.js: 'scheduledSupportDays equals supportDays in every case').

TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS FIX WERE WRONG AND WERE CAUGHT BEFORE COMMIT. (1) Applying the widened day count as a flat, block-level ceiling (rather than the week's own settled, capacity-earned figure) offered early weeks more calendar days than their earned capacity supports, which corrupted the affordability ladder into dropping a 10K population's quality sessions entirely (caught by test/planMathematicsInvariants.test.js). (2) The corrected per-week version still had no floor on whether the week's OWN supporting workload could pay for the extra day at EASY_MIN_KM, reproducing the historical 'opening week came out bigger than asked' defect (a New Half opened 17km vs a locked 15km entry, +13%; caught by test/raceGoalAdmissionViability.test.js's locked-entry guard). The final version caps the widened day count at floor(week's own supportKm*supportDays / EASY_MIN_KM) -- the identical arithmetic distributeWeekVolume() itself uses to decide a day count is affordable -- and taper reads back the block's own widened figure (via mPrevScheduledSupportDays) rather than re-earning it against taper's deliberately smaller workload, so 'taper retains established frequency, only reduces load' (HQ's own instruction) holds through the widening exactly as it already held for supportDays.

THE CONSEQUENCE OF THIS SAFETY MARGIN: WIDENING ONLY EVER FIRES WHEN A WEEK HAS GENUINE, EARNED, SPARE SUPPORTING WORKLOAD TO PLACE, and no case in this matrix's population -- which is built entirely from default state, with no demonstrated running history to earn capacity from -- ever carries enough of it for a Half/Marathon week to cross that floor. Every counter in this record, including week_over_week_growth_over_10pct (descriptive), load_progression_structure_introduced_with_dose_step and long_run_shorter_than_quality, is confirmed IDENTICAL to the pre-repair figure by a full re-run of the matrix (test/audit/matrix.js) and a field-by-field diff against this record before it was edited. The repair is proven instead at the case level, directly: test/raceGoalFrequencyRepairII.test.js constructs Experienced/Advanced Half and Marathon athletes at 4/5/6 selected days with realistic multi-week volume and asserts the HARD RULE (N selected -> at least N-1 definite) holds; it also constructs a Developing/Novice Half athlete at the same selection and records, honestly, that this population's capacity ramp does not earn enough workload to reach the same floor at any tested volume or block length (byte-identical to unmodified origin/main) -- a named, pre-existing, out-of-scope gap (see the HQ report), not a defect introduced by or hidden by this repair.
